title: Worksheet — The Raven and the Fox (Class 6 CBSE English)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show working / write full sentences for the subjective questions. Total time: 30 minutes.

questions.question: Pronouns replace nouns to avoid repetition.
Direct speech is written inside ____ marks.
What does 'flatter' mean?
options: to praise excessively, often to get something
questions.answer: to praise excessively, often to get something

questions.question: What is the moral of the fable?
options: Beware of those who flatter you — they often want something.
questions.answer: Beware of those who flatter you — they often want something.

questions.question: Retell the fable in your own words in 4-5 sentences.
questions.answer: A raven sits high on a tree branch with a piece of cheese in his beak. A hungry fox below cannot climb up, so he flatters the raven, praising his beautiful feathers and asking him to sing. The raven, full of pride, opens his beak — the cheese falls. The fox grabs it and runs away, telling the raven he has voice but no sense.

questions.question: Step-by-step, describe HOW the fox tricks the raven.
questions.answer: (1) The fox sees the cheese but cannot reach it. (2) He praises the raven's appearance. (3) He suggests such a beautiful bird must have a beautiful voice too. (4) The raven, full of pride, opens his beak to caw and show off. (5) The cheese falls; the fox grabs it and runs.

questions.question: Pick out three pairs of rhyming words from the poem.
questions.answer: Examples (any three): cheese / ease; fox / rocks; refuse / news; PLOP / hop; grin / within; praise / ways.
questions.explanation: Rhyme is a key feature; many pairs work.

questions.question: Convert to direct speech: The fox told the raven that he had a beautiful voice.
questions.answer: The fox said to the raven, "You have a beautiful voice." (Or: The fox told the raven, "You have a beautiful voice.")
questions.explanation: Use quotation marks; switch pronoun and tense as needed.

questions.question: Write your own short fable (5-7 sentences) featuring a clever animal who tricks a less clever one. End with a clear moral.
questions.answer: Sample: 'A monkey saw a basket of mangoes near a careless farmer. Seeing a goat tied nearby, he called sweetly, "Brother goat, you are so noble! Please call out loudly so everyone may hear your strong voice." The proud goat began to bleat with all his might. The farmer ran to see what was wrong; the monkey quickly grabbed three mangoes and disappeared into the trees. "You have a strong voice," the monkey called as he went, "but you have not used it for yourself today." Moral: Do not be so eager for praise that you become someone else's tool.' (Many correct answers; rubric: clear plot + moral.)

questions.question: Some readers say the raven is the real hero of the fable because he learns a lesson and grows. Do you agree? Justify in 5-6 sentences.
questions.answer: Sample: The raven is not the typical 'hero' — he is tricked, loses his cheese, and is mocked. But he is also the character who LEARNS the lesson the fable wants us to learn. By the end, the raven knows that flattery hides a motive. In that sense, his loss is the reader's gain — we learn through HIS mistake. So while the fox is clever, the raven is the character we identify with and grow with. He is the hero of the lesson, even if he is the loser of the cheese. (Rubric: clear position + reasons.)
